topic: The Mystery of Superposition: Navigating the Quantum State
target_audience: Introductory Physics Students (High School Senior/Freshman University)

sections.title: The Boundary: Classical vs. Quantum
lecture_lines: Classical objects exist in one definite state at once.
A spinning coin represents a blur of possible states.
Quantum particles exist in this "blur" as their reality.
animations: Show a binary switch flipping between '0' and '1' in white (#FFFFFF).
Transform the switch into a blurry, rotating cloud in cyan (#00FFFF).
Display the text 'SUPERPOSITION' in bold cyan (#00FFFF) above the cloud.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Vector as a State
lecture_lines: In physics, we represent a system's state as a vector.
North and East are two distinct, base directions.
A diagonal arrow combines both directions into one state.
animations: Draw a white arrow (#FFFFFF) pointing up [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/north.svg], labeled '|0>'.
Draw a second white arrow (#FFFFFF) pointing right, labeled '|1>'.
Fade in a yellow arrow (#FFFF00) pointing diagonally between the two basis arrows, using a compass [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg] as a reference frame.

sections.title: Defining Superposition (The Ket Notation)
lecture_lines: We use "ket" notation to label quantum states.
The state psi is a sum of two possibilities.
Coefficients alpha and beta scale these base states.
Schr\u00f6dinger\u2019s cat is both alive and dead simultaneously.
Superposition mathematically blends these two outcomes together.
animations: Display the symbol '|ψ>' in the center in bright green (#00FF00).
Show the components '|0>' and '|1>' appearing on either side of a plus sign.
Add coefficients 'α' and 'β' in front of the basis states.
Fade in the full equation '|ψ> = α|0> + β|1>' in green (#00FF00).
Overlay two semi-transparent cat icons [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png]: one standing and one lying down.

sections.title: Visualizing the Math: The Bloch Sphere
lecture_lines: We can map quantum states onto a 3D sphere.
The North Pole represents the pure state zero.
The South Pole represents the pure state one.
Any point on the surface is a unique superposition.
The equator marks a perfect fifty-fifty mix of states.
animations: Create a 3D-looking wireframe sphere in light gray (#CCCCCC).
Highlight the North Pole with a green dot (#00FF00) labeled '|0>'.
Highlight the South Pole with a magenta dot (#FF00FF) labeled '|1>'.
Draw a glowing yellow ring (#FFFF00) around the sphere's equator.
Animate a blue pulse (#0000FF) traveling from the equator to a point on the surface.

sections.title: The Collapse: Observation and Probability
lecture_lines: Measuring a quantum system forces a definite choice.
The superposition "collapses" into one single base state.
Amplitudes determine the likelihood of each specific outcome.
Square the coefficient to find the probability of collapse.
Once observed, the "blur" of possibilities instantly vanishes.
animations: Show a vector on the equator of the Bloch sphere vibrating rapidly.
Display a white eye icon (#FFFFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eye.svg] representing 'Measurement'.
The equatorial vector instantly snaps to the North Pole in green (#00FF00).
Display the text 'P(0) = |α|²' in green (#00FF00) near the pole.
Fade out the rest of the sphere, leaving only the North Pole highlighted.

sections.title: Application: The Power of Parallelism
lecture_lines: Classical bits are limited to zero or one.
Qubits explore multiple computational paths at the same time.
This massive parallelism solves complex problems exponentially faster.
animations: Show a single red dot (#FF0000) moving through a simple maze grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/maze.svg].
Show a wave of blue dots (#0000FF) expanding to fill all maze paths [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/maze.svg] at once.
Highlight the exit in gold (#FFD700) as the blue wave reaches it instantly within the maze [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/maze.svg].
